reasoning: The proposal's exact question—whether a judge's stated confidence is calibrated under debate vs consultancy on QuALITY, and whether abstaining on low-confidence items raises retained-set accuracy (the accuracy/coverage tradeoff)—is directly answered by published work. Khan et al. 2024 (ICML, "Debating with More Persuasive LLMs") computes judge calibration (ECE, Brier) for debate vs consultancy on QuALITY, finding debate yields lower Brier scores; reported QuALITY ECE of 0.11. Rahman et al. 2025 (ICML, "AI Debate Aids Assessment of Controversial Claims") explicitly thresholds by judge confidence, rejects low-confidence judgements, and reports the exact accuracy/coverage tradeoff (e.g., rejecting confidences below 75% retains 65% of questions at 94% accuracy), with debate beating consultancy at all coverage rates. Kenton et al. 2024 (NeurIPS, "Scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs") covers the weak-open-judge angle on QuALITY with reliability calibration. The only minor unexplored specificity is using Llama-3-8B precisely and computing separate reliability diagrams, but the problem itself—including the abstention recovery and weak-judge framing—is fully solved.

evidence.title: AI Debate Aids Assessment of Controversial Claims
evidence.summary: Directly implements confidence thresholding/abstention: rejecting judgements below a confidence threshold raises retained accuracy, with debate outperforming consultancy at all coverage rates (e.g. <75% confidence rejected retains 65% of questions at 94% accuracy). Reports Brier scores showing debate is better calibrated (0.231 vs 0.335 consultancy). This is essentially the proposed contribution.

evidence.title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers
evidence.summary: Computes judge calibration (ECE, Brier) for LLM and human judges in debate vs consultancy on QuALITY; finds debate improves calibration (QuALITY ECE 0.11) and lower Brier scores. Establishes the calibration comparison the proposal sets out to make.

evidence.title: On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs
evidence.summary: Studies weak LLM judges (including Llama-scale) judging stronger debaters/consultants on QuALITY-based extractive QA, with reliability scores calibrated on a small gold set. Covers the weak-open-judge framing central to the proposal.

evidence.title: GPT-3.5 judges can supervise GPT-4o debaters in capability asymmetric debates
evidence.summary: Community replication showing weak judges over transcripts from stronger debaters on QuALITY-style tasks, confirming the weak-judge-over-strong-transcripts setup is already explored.

evidence.title: Two-Turn Debate Doesn't Help Humans Answer Hard Reading Comprehension Questions
evidence.summary: Explores judge abstention under debate, finding judges are least likely to be incorrect when shown arguments and encouraged to abstain—directly relevant to the abstention-recovers-accuracy hypothesis.
